subject: MSA: cap & exclusions — prepaid proration and wind-down support
messages:
From: Gina Larson <gina.larson@acme-analytics.com>

Cc: Peter Hughes <peter.hughes@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Jan 2027 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: MSA: limitation of liability + termination refund carveouts

Ava —

Thanks for the draft MSA. Our legal team is comfortable with the majority of terms but has two sticking points we need to resolve before procurement can sign: the aggregate cap and the interaction between the cap/exclusions and termination/right to refund for prepaid fees. High level: we can live with a cap at 3x fees for direct damages, but we need (i) an carve-out to preserve refund rights for prepaid credits (or a clear proration mechanism) and (ii) explicit wind-down assistance obligations if you terminate for convenience or the contract is ended without cause.

Specific asks:
- Confirm whether the LoL cap applies to refunds of prepaid amounts or if those remain outside the cap.
- If prepaid fees are subject to the cap, provide an example calculation (proration approach) — our finance team wants clarity to avoid write-offs.
- We need a narrow carve-out for claims arising from your gross negligence or intentional misconduct to be outside the cap.
- Wind-down assistance: we expect 30 days of transition support (data export, handover calls) with defined SLAs and a limited credit if not met.

Please loop in your legal if needed. Procurement wants to close by the end of next week.

Best,
Gina

Subject: Re: MSA: limitation of liability + termination refund carveouts

Gina —

Thanks for the clear note. Appreciate the specificity — helps a lot. High level reply: we generally treat prepaid balances as subject to the LoL cap to keep overall commercial risk symmetric, but we can offer either (A) an explicit proration formula for refunds on termination or (B) a carve-out limited to refunds for unused prepaid term where Redwood elects to terminate for convenience.

Monica (legal) is cc'd and will propose precise redline language. Proposed operational compromise while legal aligns: if termination is initiated by either party without cause, prepaid amounts will be prorated on a daily basis for remaining unused term; any refund or credit due to customer will be treated as a monetary remedy and counted against the aggregate cap, except that refunds resulting from Redwood gross negligence or intentional misconduct will be outside the cap.

We can also include an explicit 15–30 day wind-down assistance obligation (we typically offer 15 days standard, 30 days as a paid add-on). Can you confirm whether Acme expects 30 days as a hard requirement (no fee) or as a preferred term?

I'll get you a redline from Monica by Monday.

Thanks,

Folks — forwarding Acme legal's email (below). Procurement wants to close next week. Quick thoughts before we send a redline:

- Commercial: they asked for 30d wind-down at no cost. Recommend we hold firm at 15d included, offer 30d as a professional-service item (or a credit schedule).
- Cap: they want clarity that prepaid refunds are outside the cap — I think we should push refunds within the cap but carve out gross negligence and intentional misconduct. Keeps our balance sheet predictable.
- Example: they explicitly requested a proration example for their finance team. Legal should add a small math example in the Order Form (e.g., prepaid $120k for 12 months -> 90 days used -> refund = (remaining days/total days) * prepaid).
- Escalation: If they push hard on 30d no-cost, loop in me and Rishi (sales exec) for potential commercial concession (small onboarding credit).

Can you draft a redline that: (1) includes an explicit proration formula in the Order Form, (2) states refunds are monetary remedies counted against the aggregate cap, (3) carves out gross negligence/intentional misconduct, and (4) defines wind-down assistance 15d included with optional 30d paid?

Thanks — short turnaround.

— Ava

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Fwd: MSA: limitation of liability + termination refund carveouts — draft redline attached

Team — attaching a concise redline we'll send to Acme. Key legal positions included in the document and summarized below.

1) Aggregate cap: proposed cap at the greater of (a) 3x Fees paid in the prior 12 months, or (b) $5,000,000 — preserves predictability for large customers.

2) Refunds/proration: added explicit proration formula in Order Form: Refund = Prepaid Fees * (Remaining Days / Total Days in Prepaid Term). Added an illustrative example. We state that refunds are monetary remedies and will be applied against the aggregate cap.

3) Carve-outs: preserved carve-out for claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence and intentional misconduct. Narrowly tailored — not a broad unlimited carve-out.

4) Wind-down assistance: included 15 days of reasonable transition assistance at no charge (data export, copy of logs, two handover calls). Added option for 30 days as a paid service or as part of a premium SLA addendum. If Acme insists on 30 days at no charge, recommend a small onboarding/termination credit instead of unlimited free services.

5) Operational SLA credit: proposed a capped credit equal to 10% of one month’s prepay for a failure to meet wind-down SLAs — this is both a remedy and keeps exposure limited.

I flagged the clauses in the MSA and added a short paragraph in the Order Form (section 4) that contains the proration math and an example, so procurement has a single place to look.

Attaching: MSA_Redline_ava_v2.docx (redline) and OrderForm_Acme_2027-01.pdf (with example).

If this aligns, I’ll send to Gina with a suggested note offering the draft language and asking whether they want 30d no-cost (and if so, what commercial concession they'd consider acceptable).

— Monica

Subject: Proposed compromise on cap/proration and wind-down — MSA redline attached

Gina / Peter —

Thanks again for the flagged items. Monica and I discussed and attached a concise redline that we think addresses Acme's commercial concerns while keeping Redwood's exposure bounded. Summary of the compromise: 

1) Cap: Aggregate cap at the greater of (a) 3x Fees paid in the prior 12 months, or (b) $5,000,000.
2) Refunds: Prepaid refunds will be calculated using a simple proration formula included in the Order Form. Refunds are monetary remedies and will be applied against the aggregate cap.
3) Carve-out: Claims arising from Redwood gross negligence or intentional misconduct are excluded from the cap.
4) Wind-down assistance: 15 days of transition assistance included at no charge (data export, two handover calls, minimal runbook). We added an option to elect 30 days of transition assistance as a paid professional-services line on the Order Form.
5) SLA credit: A narrowly-tailored credit is included for failure to deliver wind-down assistance per the SLA (capped at 10% of one month’s prepaid fees).

Practical note: to avoid ambiguity for your finance team, we inserted a worked example into the Order Form (see page 2) showing proration math for a 12-month prepay and a mid-term termination.

If this is acceptable, Monica can circulate a clean MSA and Order Form for signature via DocuSign and Rishi and I will coordinate any commercial credit if Acme prefers 30d at no cost.

Next steps: please let us know by end of week whether you want to (A) accept the redline as-is, or (B) counter with a 30d no-cost ask (and if so, propose what commercial concession you’ll need).

Best,
